top.line: A tour of the twin: thirteen refunds, four designs
top.para: The Northstar twin runs Ashish Rajan's retailer as a store: thirteen synthetic refunds through four designs of ten controls, every decision played, replayed and compared, or rebuilt with your own controls. This tour goes tab by tab and case by case, then explains the engine and what a twin means here.

in-short.line: Every decision plays back, tagged by pillar and policy
in-short.para: His store as a twin in a vault: four designs and ten controls, each step tagged with its question and its policy, two views of the world side by side, no model called so runs replay exactly, and one content file to swap for another process.

open.line: The page, the vault, or the command line
open.para: Play it inline on the twin's page, open the vault full screen read-only, or clone it with the public read key. The app has seven tabs, from the case to what is in the vault.

designs.line: Each design adds controls; tick your own
designs.para: A has the $200 limit and logs; B binds tools to the sender, caps at what was paid, pauses bursts and re-approves above $200; C verifies the amount and reconciles; D lets the workflow pay the decided amount, routes by amount and keeps precedents. Untick any control and the day reruns.

play.line: Step through a case beside the records
play.para: Pick a design and a case and press Play: steps appear one by one along eight workflow stages, coloured by outcome and tagged by pillar and policy. Beside them, what the agent did and what the records say, the ledger, and the trace or decision record.

n1001.para: In A the $150 is paid, $30 over. In B the cap refuses it and the customer owed $120 gets nothing. In C a person pays $120 after a mismatch. In D the rules decide $120, the workflow pays it, and the agent's $150 is recorded as a difference.

cases.line: Each case tests a control, and finds its edge
cases.para: A $260 refund refused with nobody owning it; a $199 instruction hidden in a message; the right name on the wrong order; $132 that a cap at what was paid cannot tell from $120; $261 split into three under the limit; a discount applied twice; a retry loop paying six times.

casebook.line: A precedent set, followed, then distinguished
casebook.para: Three customers want to keep damaged items, and no rule covers it. A person decides the first at 30% and it becomes precedent P-1. The next, with the same material facts, follows it with no person. A $150 jacket with a broken zip differs in a way that matters and goes back to a person.

policies.line: The three policies, and his four questions
policies.para: One tab shows the behaviour policy's rows, the decision table for who decides the amount, and the workflow's stages with their controls. Another puts each of his questions beside our answer and the controls that carry it.

built.line: One app, one engine, one content file
built.para: The engine runs the cases in order: lookup, propose, check, decide, pay, reconcile, record, carrying ledgers and precedents from case to case. It is deterministic and calls no model; the agent's mistakes are scripted, so every run replays exactly and anyone can check it.

twin.line: A copy of a process, to run decisions through
twin.para: Here a twin copies a refund process, its records, rules, controls and people's decisions, not a real store, and says nothing about how often agents err. It shows what each control catches, misses and costs. Swap the content to make one for your own process.

series.line: The reply, this tour, and the twin
series.para: The reply makes the argument, this tour walks the vault, and the twin is there to play.

limits.para: Orders, people and amounts are invented apart from Northstar's three numbers; each mistake is chosen to test a control; the minutes are assumptions; and a refund is, as his post says, a relatively simple example.

sources.line: His article, and the twin built from it
sources.para: Ashish Rajan's article and post, and the twin built by this site's agent on 18 October 2026, published with a public read key; the screenshots and numbers come from its app and engine.
